title: Fela Gets His Door

mood.label: Uneasy calm
mood.summary: Uneasy calm (44): strikes traded over Qeshm and Bahrain, drones at the Kerch bridge, Gaza's ceasefire fraying, and the US lost its measles-free status. But Fela Kuti entered the Rock Hall and a flight to Auckland returned after 26 years.

style.genre: minor afrobeat — tenor sax stabs, organ, congas, agogo, Korg M1

sampleSources: Strudel default library (VCSL staccato tenor sax, Renaissance full organ, conga, agogo bells; Korg M1 drum machine), sine-oscillator bass and pad

lines: Drones over Bahrain, a strike on Qeshm,
the Kerch bridge shaking in the dark,
Gaza's truce is thinning at the hem,
and Kyiv still sits down to talk.
Twenty-six years we kept the measles out,
today the door swung back the other way.
Twenty-six years, a plane to Auckland's ground,
Port Moresby waves it off today.
So play it long, the way Fela played it,
horns that argue, drums that won't give in —
the hall finally opened up and said it:
the trouble's old, but so's the hymn.
